parent_line.rule: v1 results are immutable and are not reinterpreted by BAM v2

scientific_question: When true biogeographic distributions are generated by explicit Abiotic, Biotic and Movement constraints, which BAM mechanisms can positive occurrences falsify, which remain non-identifiable, and what additional evidence is needed to separate them?

bam_definition.A: Abiotic suitability: nodes inside the focal species virtual environmental niche.
bam_definition.B: Biotic permissibility: nodes satisfying declared interaction rules using independently generated partner and antagonist distributions.
bam_definition.M: Movement accessibility: nodes reachable from the focal source under geographic step, hard barrier and finite horizon constraints, independently of A and B.

partner_species.generation: independent virtual species with its own abiotic niche, source and movement accessibility

antagonist_species.role: competitor, predator or other exclusionary interaction
antagonist_species.generation: independent virtual species with its own abiotic niche, source and movement accessibility

semantics.antagonist_exclusion: B = complement of antagonist occupied nodes
semantics.partner_and_antagonist: B = partner occupied nodes ∩ complement of antagonist occupied nodes

movement_layer.rationale: Preserve the BAM distinction between accessibility M and suitability A∩B; do not bake A or B into M in the primary v2 experiment.

candidate_world_decomposition.requirement: Every candidate world stores A, B, M and G=A∩B∩M separately; no weighted scalar collapse.

primary_hypotheses.claim: With noiseless positive occurrences sampled from true G0 and the exact BAM truth included, EOG never eliminates the true BAM world.

A false BAM world is eliminated by a positive occurrence exactly when at least one observed node lies outside its A, B or M set; the eliminated world can be attributed to the violated axis set without collapsing axes.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Any mismatch between set membership and compatibility refutes H2.

primary_hypotheses.claim: Distinct BAM decompositions with identical occupied set G=A∩B∩M cannot be distinguished by complete positive occurrence data.
primary_hypotheses.rule: If positive-only inference uniquely selects one member of an exact-G equivalence class, H3 is refuted.

primary_hypotheses.claim: If a false world has G_true ⊆ G_false, no amount of positive occurrence sampling from G_true can eliminate that false world.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Elimination of a positive-superset world by positive-only evidence refutes H4.

primary_hypotheses.claim: Under an explicitly perfect-detection equilibrium contract, surveyed negatives in G_false \ G_true can eliminate positive-superset false worlds that positive occurrences alone cannot.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Test only worlds with at least one diagnostic negative witness; failure to eliminate such worlds refutes H5.

primary_hypotheses.claim: When candidate worlds share final G but differ in source-conditioned arrival times, time-stamped positive colonisation observations can distinguish M histories that static final occurrences cannot.
primary_hypotheses.rule: Test only pairs with equal final G and at least one different predicted first-arrival time; failure to contract using a valid temporal witness refutes H6.

claim_boundary: Do not call B a generic environmental covariate; it is an explicit interaction-derived permissibility set.
Do not treat M as suitability; it is source-conditioned accessibility.
Do not claim unique historical truth when multiple BAM decompositions remain compatible.
Perfect surveyed negatives are a separate idealized evidence contract and do not transfer automatically to real presence-only data.
Temporal arrival evidence is used only when timestamps are generated from the known movement truth.

language.cpp: optional backend only after exact Python equivalence; BAM scientific definitions remain in the Python contract
